item.title: Skyrmion gears: translation-to-rotation conversion of skyrmion clusters along periodic substrates
item.description: arXiv:2610.17102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate how the translational motion of a compact skyrmion cluster can be converted into collective rotation through interactions with a periodic obstacle substrate. Using an effective particle model, we consider a seven-skyrmion cluster driven along a one-dimensional array of repulsive obstacle sites. For suitable obstacle spacings and interaction strengths, repeated interactions with the substrate produce coherent clockwise or counterclockwise rotation, giving rise to gear-like cluster dynamics. We characterize these states using the translational velocity, Hall angle, angular velocity, structural deformation, and a dimensionless gear ratio that relates cluster rotation to motion over the substrate periodicity. Dynamical phase diagrams identify rotating, nonrotating, wall-guided, transverse, and deformed regimes. We further show that coherent rotation persists in the overdamped limit, demonstrating that the conversion mechanism does not require an intrinsic Magnus force and may therefore extend to other driven cluster systems, including colloidal assemblies. These results provide a simple route for controlling collective rotation through structured substrates.
item.dc:creator: N. P. Vizarim, C. J. O. Reichhardt, C. Reichhardt

item.title: Imaging the topological sign of a Dirac mass with spin-polarized tunneling
item.description: arXiv:2610.17464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A Dirac mass is characterized not only by its magnitude but also by its sign, which influences the Berry curvature, Hall response, and the propagation direction of chiral boundary modes. However, local spectroscopy of magnetic topological surfaces has so far accessed only the gap magnitude $|M|$. Here we show how the topological sign of $M$ can be determined locally. We first establish the sign information that spin-resolved tunneling can access and the reference required to obtain an absolute Hall sign. Although spin--orbital entanglement generally obscures the relation between measured spin and Dirac pseudospin, crystalline rotation symmetry alleviates this ambiguity at the band edge. On a $C_3$ axis, an axial tip couples to a fully spin-polarized state whose tunneling asymmetry directly reveals the sign of the occupied-band Berry curvature, independent of orbital composition. We further show that the zeroth Landau level provides an independent mass-sign measurement with an unpolarized tip, while opposite domains and their chiral domain-wall modes provide self-consistency checks. These results pave the way for imaging the locations where the topological character changes within a material, rather than merely identifying where a spectral gap appears.

item.title: Mathematical framework for simulation of non-perturbative cavity optomechanics with plate-like dielectrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cavity optomechanical models typically treat a sensor either as a perturbative polarizable object in a pre-existing optical field, or solve the field at a fixed equilibrium and linearize in a fixed optical-mode basis. Neither self-consistently determines the spatially resolved cavity field, the optical force, the mechanical equilibrium, and the back-action when a finite-thickness dielectric plate intercepts the entire optical mode and restructures the intracavity field. In this companion paper to [1], we develop that treatment by extending the vacuum two-photon formalism to finite-thickness planar dielectrics, incorporating their Fresnel reflection, internal propagation, optical forces, and mechanical back-action directly into the field equations. We derive the carrier and sideband transfer functions needed to describe the coupled optical-mechanical system, including optomechanical cooling and the response to external perturbations. The result is a systematic starting point for calculating detector response and noise budgets for cavity experiments with intracavity dielectrics, including gravitational wave detectors deploying levitated sensors.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Laeuger, Nancy Aggarwal

item.title: Theory of deeply subwavelength electromagnetic structuring of semiconductors due to thermal-ionization instability
item.description: arXiv:2610.17847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a theory of ionization-assisted instability that governs the reflection of intense electromagnetic pulses from a semiconductor surface. Local overheating of the material increases the free-carrier density and conductivity, which in turn enhances the absorption of the incident radiation and further amplifies local heating and avalanche ionization. At high pump repetition rates, the overheating accumulates from pulse to pulse, leading to a gradual rise of the local material temperature and free carrier density - a positive feedback loop that drives thermal runaway. However, this effect competes with diffraction of the pump field on the emerging perturbation of the dielectric permittivity or on the surface relief, which reduces the local electric field amplitude in the overheated regions, thus providing negative feedback. We show that the competition between heat diffusion and diffraction near-field weakening creates conditions for the exponential growth of temperature perturbations with a certain wavenumber determined by the pulse repetition rate, pump field, thermal conductivity and other material parameters. The derived analytical expressions accurately describe the spatial period of deeply subwavelength structures observed in recent experiments on silicon structuring by intense terahertz radiation, and reproduce qualitatively dependencies of their period on the pump intensity, the incident wavelength and the number of pump pulses.

item.title: Emergent Non-Biorthogonal Born Rule at Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.17855v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Non-Hermitian dynamics possesses distinct left and right eigenstates, but their normalization freedom obscures a direct probabilistic interpretation. Starting from a globally Hermitian system governed by the standard Born rule, we generalize dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) from a reference state to a physical subspace. This generalization provides a clear probabilistic interpretation of left and right states: when each state is normalized to itself, their mutual overlap determines a directly accessible dynamical transition rate. We discuss the new phenomena governed by this emergent non-biorthogonal Born rule and further identify a class of exceptional-point DQPTs (EP-DQPTs), at which the eigenstates of the critical propagator coalesce. Our theory places the probabilistic interpretation of non-Hermitian quantum mechanics on the firm footing of Hermitian quantum mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Wei Yang, Henning Schomerus, Jiangping Hu, Zhesen Yang

item.title: On-chip optical isolators
item.description: arXiv:2610.17862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical isolation suppresses back-reflections that destabilize lasers, produce parasitic interference, and increase crosstalk in photonic systems. Although free-space and fibre-optic isolators are mature, no broadly adopted on-chip technology yet combines strong isolation, low insertion loss, broad bandwidth, compact footprint, and scalable fabrication. The difficulty is twofold: Lorentz reciprocity must be broken, and every relevant backward spatial, spectral, and polarization channel must be suppressed. This Review develops a common framework for assessing proposed solutions. We first distinguish pairwise nonreciprocity from intensity-asymmetric transmission and from true isolation using the constitutive relations and scattering matrix. We then compare three physical routes to an integrated nonreciprocal response: magneto-optical bias, externally driven space-time modulation, and nonlinear optical processes. Topological and non-Hermitian systems are treated as cross-cutting design frameworks that can route, protect, or enhance an underlying nonreciprocal response, but do not by themselves break reciprocity. Finally, we examine fundamental constraints and practical trade-offs among isolation, insertion loss, bandwidth, footprint, modal coverage, drive requirements, and fabrication compatibility. The resulting mechanism-based perspective connects reciprocity-breaking physics to the requirements of scalable photonic integrated circuits.

item.title: Direct view of exciton and carrier dynamics in twisted bilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2610.17984v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (tBLG) on H-intercalated SiC (twist angle of $9 \pm 1^{\circ}$) is studied by position\mbox{-}, time\mbox{-}, and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). Both graphene layers are hole doped, with a Dirac-point offset of 30~meV. Time-resolved ARPES near the van Hove singularity reveals a spectral feature within the hybridization-induced band gap, together with excited electrons in the conduction band. The in-gap feature exhibits distinct dynamics, and its binding energy and $k$-space location are consistent with the proposed non-hydrogenic ``ghost-Fano'' exciton arising from destructive interference between two nearly degenerate excitonic channels. Near the Dirac points, the twist separates the largely layer-polarized Dirac cones in momentum space, providing direct layer selectivity. We find markedly different peak electronic temperatures in the two graphene layers, even though their subsequent cooling dynamics are very similar. We attribute this to an ultrafast interlayer redistribution of electronic energy, driven by an interlayer electric field that arises from the different doping in the layers.

item.title: Chirality Inversion and Giant Optical Activity in Scalable Self-Assembled Metamaterials
item.description: arXiv:2610.18116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chiral materials manipulate light in ways that hold promise for sensing, imaging, and photonics, but producing such materials with strong and reproducible optical activity at large scale remains challenging. Here, we develop a scalable strategy to assemble hierarchical helicoidal metamaterials from metallic nanoparticles and chitin nanocrystals, a biosourced polysaccharide. Spontaneous co-assembly produces ordered chiral structures with strong plasmonic optical activity, reaching a dissymmetry factor of 0.55. The unprecedented ability to vary the helicoidal pitch allows control of the optical response, enabling inversion of optical handedness without changing the handedness of the template, effectively decoupling geometrical chirality from optical chirality. Remarkably, the gold nanoparticles can also be recovered from dry films and redispersed as colloids, introducing an appealing circularity concept for sustainable chiral plasmonic materials.

item.title: Non-Hermitian Statistical Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.18175v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Particle exchange in two dimensions gives rise to quantum statistics beyond the boson-fermion dichotomy, with central roles in fractional quantum Hall physics, topological quantum computation, and strongly correlated quantum matter. In conventional topological phases, microscopic exchange geometry is compressed into rigid braid and fusion data. We develop a theory of non-Hermitian statistical geometry in which relaxing Hermiticity softens these exchange data into a larger complex space of spectral and relative-geometric degrees of freedom. For two adjacent braid generators, a single projective exchange spectrum is insufficient: their relative eigenline geometry supplies an additional gauge-invariant modulus. On the generic irreducible two-channel branch, braid consistency locks these coordinates through an exact spectrum-geometry relation. Using Riesz projectors and Kato transport, we realize this geometry in a five-arm Kitaev-Majorana network and test spectral and relative-geometric responses in an independent two-dimensional four-vortex Kitaev model. Finite-time dynamics tests the exchange operation, microscopic fusion sewing tests its composition across fusion descriptions, and matched-spectrum controls isolate the role of relative geometry. Nonzero projective Kato curvature shows that braid-consistent, fusion-coherent exchange can depend on the control path. Non-Hermiticity thus exposes exchange geometry, braid consistency re-locks it, fusion coherence further constrains it, and projective flatness determines when geometric exchange becomes intrinsically topological.

item.title: A Topological Spin on Racetrack Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.18297v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic racetrack memory requires localized carriers that combine rapid motion, resistance to perturbations and a detectable signal. Here we show how a 360{\deg} domain wall in a hollow ferromagnetic tube combines these properties within a single continuous magnetic shell. Two successive magnetization reversals form a bound object whose surrounding domains point in the same direction. Analytical energetics and micromagnetic simulations establish its finite separation, recovery from tested perturbations and current driven transport without microscopic Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction or a maintaining field. The texture's winding resists unwinding while radial rotation carries an energy cost, providing a specific control over stability. Relative rotation of the constituent spins accounts quantitatively for additional displacement during current onset. The wall supports motion at hundreds of metres per second, with transient velocities approaching one kilometre per second at stronger drive. A prepared seven-bit pattern retains its carriers and local readout contrast after pulsed transport and recovery. Curved-track and differential-current tests identify radial stiffness and drive uniformity as controls for intact motion. These results establish a physical basis for fast, locally distinguishable tubular magnetic bits and identify a continuous switching pathway that can be targeted by tailored excitation.

item.title: Altermagnetic Ground States on the Ammann--Beenker Tiling
item.description: arXiv:2610.18441v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify exact altermagnetic ground states of a classical Heisenberg model on a quasicrystal. Considering the Ammann--Beenker tiling as an example, we determine the ground states by exploiting the parity structure of its parent four-dimensional hypercubic lattice. The ground state hosts coplanar altermagnetic order characterized by the preserved spin-group symmetry $[C_{2x}\parallel C_{8z}]$. Without translational symmetry, the momentum-space spin splitting that usually identifies altermagnets is not directly accessible. We instead couple the spins to itinerant electrons and show spin-resolved transport with $g$-wave symmetry, confirming the altermagnetic nature in a nonperiodic system. Our results establish a geometric route to altermagnetic order in quasicrystals, connecting exact magnetic ground states to their spin-resolved transport signatures.
item.dc:creator: SeungBeom Hong, YunHo Kim, Moon Jip Park, GiBaik Sim

item.title: Quantitative Modelling of Solvation in 2D Materials via Alchemical Decoupling and Potential Energy Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18490v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding why 2D materials remain suspended in solutions is essential to understanding the mechanisms of aggregation and exfoliation. These dynamics have been difficult to model because of the long timescales and large activation energies involved in these simulations. Here we describe an improved strategy for modelling the solvation and stability of 2D materials that uses the Gibbs free energy of solvation to accurately calibrate two disconnected potential energy surfaces for the fully desolvated and fully solvated 2D materials. By joining these surfaces using solvation energy, we obtain predictions for 2D material stability in various solvents that are qualitatively different than prior simulations and that have excellent agreement with experimental results. Our approach predicts a much higher barrier to full desolvation of the material, suggesting that materials that appear to be aggregated in fact still retain monolayers of solvent between adjacent layers of 2D materials. This work provides much needed understanding on the interactions between the solvent and 2D material that can guide future experimental work.
item.dc:creator: Lindsey N. Ioos, Duncan A. Peterson, Scott C. Warren

item.title: Ring states in topological materials
item.description: arXiv:2406.03529v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ingap states in semiconductors are commonly characterized by hydrogenic models within the effective mass approximation. However, when impurities are strong, this description fails. The bound states are non-perturbative with energy pinned to a zero of the impurity-projected Green's function. We show that in the presence of Wannier obstructions, such zeros are irremovable. That is, no symmetric, gap-preserving deformation of the bulk can return the ingap state to the band continuum. We call these states ring states: their wavefunctions show a node at the impurity site, and their mixed band character is set by minimizing the level repulsion exerted by the bands above and below the gap. In Chern insulators, the band mixing endows occupied ring states with local circulating currents, remnant of a small edge mode surrounding the vacancies. Clusters of vacancies bind ring states that hybridize to form dispersive chiral edge modes, providing a real-space view of bulk-boundary correspondence.
item.dc:creator: Raquel Queiroz, Roni Ilan, Zhida Song, B. Andrei Bernevig, Ady Stern

item.title: Two-dimensional Topological Quantum Chemistry and Catalog of Topological Materials
item.description: arXiv:2411.08950v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-dimensional topological materials host symmetry-protected, disorder-robust edge states cen- tral to quantum technologies. Yet, they remain scarce compared with their three-dimensional coun- terparts. We adapt the topological quantum chemistry formalism to layer groups, and study the band topology of 8,872 entries from the computational materials databases C2DB and MC2D. We find 4,073 topological or obstructed entries, including 905 topological insulators and 1,003 obstructed atomic insulators, greatly expanding the library of such materials in two dimensions. Detailed elec- tronic and topological properties of all materials are compiled into a a Topological 2D Materials Database (2D-TQCDB), and the edge states of selected new materials are studied in detail. Our methodology is implemented in new publicly available programs, designed to study the topology of any non-magnetic monolayer or multilayer material.
item.dc:creator: Urko Petralanda, Yi Jiang, Hanqi Pi, Maia G. Vergniory, B. Andrei Bernevig, Nicolas Regnault, Luis Elcoro

item.title: Observation of Altermagnetic Spin Splitting in an Intercalated Transition Metal Dichalcogenide
item.description: arXiv:2508.12985v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Altermagnetism is a novel magnetic phase combining characteristics of both antiferromagnetism and ferromagnetic ordering. Despite growing theoretical interest in altermagnetic materials, reports of experimentally verified high Neel temperature layered compounds are limited or remain to be firmly established. Here, we present an angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and density functional theory (DFT) study of Co1/4TaSe2, a compound we identify as a layered altermagnetic material. Magnetic susceptibility measurements confirm type A antiferromagnetic ordering with a Neel temperature of 178 K. Our ARPES measurements reveal an electronic band structure in excellent agreement with DFT calculations, demonstrating clear signatures of altermagnetic spin splitting at the Fermi surface. Furthermore, temperature dependent ARPES reveals a reconstructed valence band structure, with observable band shifts and the closing of energy gaps upon heating above the Neel temperature (TN), consistent with the suppression of altermagnetic order. These findings establish Co1/4TaSe2 as a promising platform for exploring altermagnetic phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Milo Sprague, Mazharul Islam Mondal, Anup Pradhan Sakhya, Resham Babu Regmi, Surasree Sadhukhan, Arun K. Kumay, Himanshu Sheokand, Igor I. Mazin, Nirmal J. Ghimire, Madhab Neupane

item.title: Anyonic time exchange in hierarchical Hall states: emergent Luttinger scaling and cross-correlations at finite temperature
item.description: arXiv:2510.20592v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We address hierarchical fractional quantum Hall edges coupled by a spatially local quantum point contact within the Unified Nonequilibrium Perturbative (UNEP) framework. Without assuming a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid (TLL) tunneling correlator, we impose a local anyonic time-exchange (ATE) constraint with phase $\bar{\theta}$, yielding a nonequilibrium fluctuation-dissipation integral equation relating DC tunneling current and noise. For thermal initial states, detailed balance closes this equation for the current. Using the Wiener-Hopf method, we find a unique physical solution of local TLL form, with scaling dimension $\delta$ determined by $\bar{\theta}=\pi\delta\pmod{\pi}$, emerging from the solution rather than being imposed via a TLL correlator. By contrast, ATE and inversion symmetry alone fix the exchange monodromy but not the full transport dynamics. We then study the "anyon collider" beyond Laughlin states at finite temperatures. Detailed balance is broken and noise becomes super-Poissonian, but the relation between nonequilibrium and equilibrium correlators determines current and noise. The output cross-correlation and balanced generalized Fano factor depend on both $\delta$ and statistical phase $\theta$, identical to $\bar{\theta}$ for co-propagating modes with short-range interactions. A temperature-dependent current scale separates the zero-temperature asymptotic regime from the low-current regime, where the balanced Fano factor saturates to a function of $\theta$ and $\delta$ distinct from its zero-temperature value. This latter regime is particularly relevant to ``anyon collider'' experiments. These complementary regimes constrain the statistical phase and scaling dimension, subject to the symmetry $\delta\mapsto1-\delta$ at fixed $\theta$. For independent statistical phase and scaling dimension, the thermal crossover can reverse the sign of output cross-correlations.
item.dc:creator: Aleksander Latyshev, Ines Safi

item.title: Fano profile in the resonance fluorescence spectrum of a solid-state quantum emitter coupled to phonons
item.description: arXiv:2512.19435v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a theory of resonance fluorescence (RF) of a solid-state quantum emitter in the regime of weak optical excitation. The emitter is coupled to the phonon modes of the surrounding bulk semiconductor, described by a super-Ohmic spectral density. We show that the RF spectrum of this system consists of a central elastic line, a broad phonon sideband known from other linear and non-linear spectra of such systems, and a narrow inelastic contribution characteristic of scattering spectra, stemming from noise-induced transient dynamics. At moderate phonon couplings or low temperatures, the interplay between the broad sideband and the inelastic feature leads to a Fano-like profile near the resonant energy with the Fano parameter determined by laser detuning. In the weak-coupling limit (where only single-phonon processes are included), the spectrum becomes an exact Fano shape, with the inelastic component vanishing completely at the exact laser frequency. The amplitude of this spectral feature grows linearly with temperature, while its width depends solely on the spontaneous emission rate of the emitter. Because the spectral line shape is extremely sensitive to dephasing, resonance fluorescence can serve as a direct, non-interferometric probe of coherence at dephasing rates critical for generating highly indistinguishable single photons. We relate the quantum character of the reservoir to the non-commutativity of noise observables and show that the Fano resonance persists in the classical (commutative) limit. We also discuss how the redistribution of optical coupling efficiency between the central line and the sidebands affects the total scattering rate under various excitation conditions.
item.dc:creator: Rafal A. Bogaczewicz, Pawel Machnikowski

item.title: Geometry-Enforced Topological Chiral Fermions in Amorphous Chiral Metals
item.description: arXiv:2512.19791v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Since the prediction and observation of topological Weyl semimetals (chiral TSMs), there have been enormous efforts to characterize further condensed matter realizations of chiral fermions. These efforts were dramatically accelerated by the subsequent discovery of a profound link between low-energy topological and lattice chirality in structurally chiral crystals. Though TSMs are well understood in the limit of perfect translation symmetry, real solid-state materials host defects and disorder, and may even be rendered amorphous down to all but the smallest system length scales. Previous theoretical studies have concluded that chiral TSMs transition into trivial diffusive metals at moderate disorder scales, raising concerns that chiral TSM states may only be accessible in highly crystalline samples. In this work, we in contrast identify large families of chiral TSMs that instead persist under strong structural disorder even into the amorphous regime. We show that amorphous chiral TSM phases can be stabilized in particular by the presence of long-range order in the local structural chirality. We present extensive analytic and numerical calculations demonstrating the existence of both Weyl and higher-charge chiral fermions in amorphous metals whose topology and spin and orbital angular momentum textures are tunable via the interplay of average symmetry and geometry. To distinguish and generate new realizations of strongly disordered chiral fermions, we introduce an analytic approach grounded in symmetry group theory. We then introduce an amorphous Wilson loop numerical method to identify chiral fermions in metals with 3D structural disorder. Our findings bridge the crystalline and strongly disordered regimes of chiral TSMs, and indicate a clear route toward engineering geometry-enforced topology in noncrystalline materials and metamaterials.
item.dc:creator: Justin Schirmann, Adolfo G. Grushin, Benjamin J. Wieder

item.title: Geometry-Induced Skin Effect in Electron Hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2601.17229v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In ultra-clean 2d materials electron viscosity is as important as Ohmic dissipation and electron transport exhibits hydrodynamic features. Using a simple framework of Brinkman equations we find that hydrodynamic electron flows give rise to a geometric skin effect: sharp obstacles locally enhance the current suppressing it far from the edges where the flow is unobstructed. This effect arises within hydrodynamic transport with finite momentum relaxation and does not rely on ballistic dynamics. Our results provide a natural hydrodynamic interpretation of edge-enhanced and double-bump current profiles observed in constricted geometries. By comparing with recent scanning NV magnetometry experiments on gated graphene, we demonstrate that such flow patterns are consistent with viscous hydrodynamics shaped by geometry, clarifying the role of geometric effects in the interpretation of electronic flow experiments.
item.dc:creator: Jaros{\l}aw Paw{\l}owski, Piotr Sur\'owka, Konstantin Zarembo

item.title: Quasicrystal Architected Nanomechanical Resonators via Data-Driven Design
item.description: arXiv:2604.07379v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: From butterfly wings to remnants of nuclear detonation, aperiodic order repeatedly emerges in nature, often exhibiting reduced sensitivity to boundaries and symmetry constraints. Inspired by this principle, a paradigm shift is introduced in nanomechanical resonator design from periodic to aperiodic structures, focusing on a special class: quasicrystals (QCs). Although soft clamping enabled by phononic stopbands has become a central strategy for achieving high-$Q_m$ nanomechanical resonators, its practical realization has been largely confined to periodic phononic crystals, where band structure engineering is well established. The potential of aperiodic architectures, however, has remained largely unexplored, owing to their intrinsic complexity and the lack of systematic approaches to identifying and exploiting stopband behavior. Here we demonstrate that soft clamping can be realized in quasicrystal architectures and that high-$Q_m$ nanomechanical resonators can be systematically predicted through a data-driven design framework. As a representative demonstration, the 12-fold QC-based resonator obtained numerically a quality factor $Q_m \sim 10^7$ and an effective mass of sub-nanograms at MHz frequencies, corresponding to an exceptional force sensitivity of $26.4$~aN/$\sqrt{\text{Hz}}$ compared to previous 2D phononic crystals. These results establish QCs as a robust platform for next-generation nanomechanical resonators and open a new design regime beyond periodic order.
item.dc:creator: Kawen Li, Hangjin Cho, Richard Norte, Dongil Shin

item.title: Femtosecond tunneling spectroscopy of ultrafast band bending dynamics at the atomic limit
item.description: arXiv:2604.25146v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Atomic-scale disorder shapes the potential energy landscape traversed by photocarriers, while the carriers themselves also dynamically reshape this landscape. However, resolving ultrafast photocarrier motion at atomic length scales has remained a central challenge in materials science. Here, we demonstrate that lightwave-driven terahertz scanning tunnelling microscopy (THz-STM) provides access to these dynamics by probing the ultrafast evolution of local electronic structure following resonant interband excitation. We introduce a generalized inversion protocol that reconstructs the time-dependent differential conductance directly from measured THz-STM data, enabling quantitative analysis of the photoexcited electronic structure without prior knowledge of the sample's properties. Applying this approach to the photoexcited GaAs(110) surface, we image the resulting femtosecond carrier dynamics by tracking the transient photocurrents produced by ultrafast shifts in the energy alignment of surface and bulk electronic states near individual surface defects. The reconstructed dynamics reveal time-dependent band bending induced by the photocarriers and highlight three key mechanisms that contribute to the ultrafast tunnel current response. Critically, terahertz time-domain sampling of the tip near-field, which both captures the waveform and demonstrates its invariance under sample photoexcitation, allows the intrinsic sample dynamics to be disentangled from the coherent sub-cycle dynamics induced by the terahertz driving field. We establish a new regime of ultrafast tunnelling spectroscopy that captures transient electronic structure and dynamic band alignment with unprecedented spatio-temporal resolution, which has significant implications for understanding carrier transport, defect-mediated processes, and the development of optoelectronic technologies based on dynamically tunable materials.
item.dc:creator: Kaedon Cleland-Host, Vedran Jelic, Stefanie Adams, Mohamed A. Hassan, Jacob M. Conley, Austin Hayes, Sheng H. Lee, Tyler L. Cocker

item.title: Breakdown of Fluctuational Electrodynamics in the Extreme Near Field
item.description: arXiv:2606.05845v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fluctuational electrodynamics relies on the assumption that thermal fluctuations in distinct bodies are statistically independent. It is shown that this approximation breaks down in the extreme near-field regime, where hybridization of surface phonon-polaritons across nanometric vacuum gaps generates finite fluctuating-current cross correlations between opposite interfaces. Using a microscopic coupled-oscillator model combined with a Green-tensor formulation of the Poynting vector, the resulting correlation-induced correction to radiative heat transfer is derived. For polar materials, these correlations become significant when the hybridization energy approaches the intrinsic damping rate and can substantially modify conventional fluctuational-electrodynamics predictions at subnanometric separations.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Ben-Abdallah

item.title: Electron state tomography from quasiparticle interference maps
item.description: arXiv:2606.18858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Characterizing electronic band structures requires precise knowledge of wave functions and their quantum geometry. Here, we introduce a tomography method to reconstruct the density matrix of electron states from quasiparticle interference maps around single impurities. We consider two-orbital models on a honeycomb lattice, relevant to graphene heterostructures and direct-gap semiconductors. For on-site impurities, backscattering between time-reversed states directly maps the density matrix populations and coherences into distinct orbital contributions in the interference map. While local probes usually lack orbital resolution, these orbital contributions transform under distinct symmetry group representations and can thus be disentangled to reveal the density matrix and quantum geometric tensor of the scattering states. This establishes impurities as tomographic probes for band structures in scanning tunneling microscopy using conventional, unpolarized tips.
item.dc:creator: A. Razanajatovo, J. Cayssol, C. Dutreix

item.title: Fingerprints of an Imbert-Fedorov-like effect in the tunneling transmission of Rarita-Schwinger semi-metals
item.description: arXiv:2606.23095v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study tunneling through a square barrier in a rotationally symmetric Rarita-Schwinger semi-metal and identify fingerprints of an Imbert-Fedorov-like effect in the tunneling transmission. The problem is intrinsically multichannel at all energies because there exist two propagating sectors with spin projections $m=1/2$ and $m=3/2$. We derive the transmission amplitudes analytically and compare the single-channel and coherent mixed-incidence cases in the two channels. Interestingly, we observe that tunneling at high energy shows a bias towards scattering into spin projection $3/2$ contributions. For single-channel injection, we find that the transmission remains symmetric under a mirror transformation of the incident angle. In contrast, for the coherent superposition, we find a directional asymmetry in the transmission probability $T(k_y)\neq T(-k_y)$. Importantly, this effect does not originate from an anisotropy of the dispersion. Instead, it arises from the phase structure of the multicomponent scattering states. The two spin projection sectors exhibit different scattering and barrier-propagation phases, which enter as interference terms when both channels appear as a coherent superposition. This interference term is identified as the cause of the broken mirror symmetry. We therefore discover an analog of the Imbert-Fedorov effect, at the level of interface-induced phase differences between internal wave components. Our result demonstrates that asymmetric tunneling can already occur in transport experiments, even in an idealized, isotropic multiband system, and should therefore not be automatically attributed solely to explicit band anisotropy.
item.dc:creator: Otman Bouladiane, Ahmed Jellal, Hocine Bahlouli, A. Al Luhaibi, Michael Vogl

item.title: Andreev exceptional points in Josephson junctions formed by minimal Kitaev chains
item.description: arXiv:2606.23956v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider Josephson junctions formed by two minimal Kitaev chains and investigate how the interplay between non-Hermiticity and superconducting phase difference enables the realization of stable topological states that do not exist in the Hermitian realm. In particular, we focus on non-Hermiticity produced by coupling the minimal Kitaev chain Josephson junction to normal reservoirs, which renders the system open and characterized by a complex Andreev spectrum. Interestingly, we find that this complex spectrum hosts second order exceptional points, where a pair of eigenvalues and their respective eigenvectors coalesce, and are fully controlled by the superconducting phase difference. Depending on the spatial unequal distribution of non-Hermiticity, these Andreev exceptional points can appear at zero or finite energies connecting stable energy lines protected by non-Hermitian topology. Moreover, tuning the system parameters, such as onsite energies, non-Hermiticity, or electron cotunneling, the Andreev exceptional points give rise to Andreev exceptional lines enclosing protected two-dimensional zero real energy areas. We also discuss potential detection schemes of Andreev exceptional points by using local and nonlocal conductance signatures. Our results demonstrate the utility of non-Hermiticity from normal reservoirs as a useful resource for engineering non-Hermitian topological phases in minimal Kitaev chain Josephson junctions.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Cayao, Masatoshi Sato

item.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
item.description: arXiv:2607.03698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^\zeta$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are connected rather than by how many are active, with the current scaling approximately as \(N^{2.3}\) while the number of active junctions grows only linearly. Contrary to the expectation that junction heterogeneity strengthens the nonlinear response, homogeneous junctions in a well-connected network produce the most abrupt and reproducible turn-on. Thus, each structural parameter acts as a distinct control knob. The mean junction characteristics set the threshold, junction uniformity sets the switching sharpness, and network density and voids set the connectivity and current. These relationships provide design rules for tailoring nanonecklace networks to a desired conduction behavior through synthesis and fabrication.
item.dc:creator: Obed Issakah, Srivathsan Badrinarayanan, Ravi F. Saraf, Janghoon Ock

item.title: Room-Temperature Nonlinear Hall Effect in Polycrystalline Magnetic Multilayers
item.description: arXiv:2607.04754v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a zero-field nonlinear Hall effect in sputtered polycrystalline Ta/Pt/[Pt/Co/Fe/Ir]$_5$/Pt multilayers from 2 to 300 K. Angle-resolved transport reveals macroscopic in-plane anisotropy and a second-order response. The transverse voltage scales quadratically with current and remains unchanged across magnetization reversal. Conductivity scaling reveals strong scattering contributions, and first-principles calculations yield a symmetry-allowed Berry curvature dipole. Our findings support a mixed intrinsic-extrinsic response and establish a scalable platform for nonlinear electronics
item.dc:creator: Preet Kamal, Amiya Mondal, Kanupriya, Chirag Kalouni, Awadhesh Narayan, Debangsu Roy

item.title: Phonons under confinement: Coarse-grained $U(1)$ charge and a new transport mechanism
item.description: arXiv:2607.14232v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An important feature of solid-state or cold atom systems in low dimensions is the restricted oscillations of ionic/atomic degrees of freedom in the confining directions, for which the conventional phonon from canonical quantization is not an ideal description. In this work we propose a general recipe to introduce this feature to otherwise unrestricted systems by mapping displacement fields to spin degrees of freedom, dubbed soft-corization. In the strong-confinement limit $S=1/2$, we demonstrate the validity of the approach with a harmonic chain; the results lead to a gapped fermionic model showing the absence of acoustic modes as a signature of the confinement of the entire chain. Despite the non-conserved total particle number in the presence of nearest-neighbor parings, the model holds a coarse-grained $U(1)$ symmetry with conserved polarization charge in the absence of nearest-neighbor hopping. This enables a new transport mechanism via "dimer-tumbling" instead of single-particle hopping. We then introduce a short-range interaction via anharmonicity; for energy scales slightly above the gap, it leads to a (quantum) phase transition to a nonreciprocal state carrying polarization charge current and heat current with spontaneous time reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) of the type $\hat{T}^2=+1$. The non-reciprocity can be probed by measuring the change of inductance due to gauge fields in and out of the ordered phase.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Gao, K. A. Muttalib

item.title: Long-range and steady-state entanglement of nitrogen vacancy centers using microwaves as a drive and synthetic antiferromagnet as a dissipator
item.description: arXiv:2607.15259v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The search for optimal schemes and dissipative environments that can mediate long-range entanglement between two distant nitrogen-vacancy centers (NVCs) in diamond has been the subject of vigorous efforts over the past decade due to potential applications of such microscopic solid-state qubits in quantum sensing and quantum computing. However, stabilizing entanglement of NVCs into a {\em steady state} poses a significant challenge, typically requiring tuning the environment {\em out of equilibrium}. Here we microscopically and rigorously derive a Lindblad quantum master equation (QME) for a system of two {\em driven-dissipative} NVCs, where the drive is microwave radiation and dissipation is provided by a single magnetic bath that is kept in {\em equilibrium}. The jump operators within the Lindblad QME are expressed in terms of Keldysh Green's functions defined as correlators of dipolar field operators of the bath. This QME makes it possible to predict precise conditions for long-range and steady-state entanglement of two NVCs, while suggesting that a synthetic antiferromagnet could be an {\em optimal} choice for a dissipative environment. By using realistic parameters from available experiments, we estimate steady-state concurrence reaching $\mathcal{C}\simeq 0.28$ for two NVCs separated by $\sim 100 \: \mathrm{nm}$.
item.dc:creator: Federico Garcia-Gaitan, Branislav K. Nikolic

item.title: Field-controlled breaking and restoration of parity-time symmetry in Josephson interference
item.description: arXiv:2608.16414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Symmetry plays a fundamental role in determining the phases and physical properties of quantum matter. Controlling symmetry in mesoscopic superconducting devices provides a route to reconfigure their phase-coherent transport. Here we demonstrate symmetry-selective Josephson interferometry in lateral NbTi/PtTe$_{\text{2}}$/NbTi junctions by controlling the relative orientations of the current and magnetic field. From the supercurrent interference patterns, we construct a field-current symmetry map that identifies configurations exhibiting or violating the device-level parity ($\mathcal{P}$), time-reversal ($\mathcal{T}$) and their combined $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry. In the absence of an in-plane field, the junction exhibits a symmetric Fraunhofer pattern. An in-plane field parallel to the current produces a pronounced side-lobe asymmetry, whereas reversing both the current and the complete magnetic-field configuration restores a generalized $\mathcal{T}$ relation. Remarkably, orienting the in-plane field perpendicular to the current restores the $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Fraunhofer response even at substantial field strengths. A microscopic model attributes this behavior to the interplay between disorder-induced potential variations and flux dipoles generated by in-plane-field Meissner focusing near the superconducting electrodes. Our results establish a reconfigurable Josephson interferometer in which the field-current geometry selects the symmetry operation being probed and switches the device between symmetry-broken and symmetry-restored interference states.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Chen Tsai, Yung-Yeh Chang, Tao-Yi Hsu, Thomas Kuo, Chia-Nung Kuo, Chin-Shan Lue, Kuei-Lin Chiu, Chen-Hsuan Hsu, Chung-Ting Ke

item.title: Multicomponent Magnetic Domain Walls in Rhombohedral Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2608.26104v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spatial textures of magnetic order, such as domain walls and skyrmions, are fundamental objects in magnetism. In rhombohedral multilayer graphene, magnetic order involves spin and valley degrees of freedom, opening the possibility of qualitatively new spatial textures. Here, we explore this possibility through a microscopic study of a one-dimensional domain wall in the valley-imbalanced quarter-metal phase of rhombohedral graphene. We uncover two different classes of domain walls. One resembles a conventional magnetic domain wall, locally rotating between the two bulk states, whereas the other is intrinsically multicomponent and explores states that are not occupied in either bulk domain. Which texture is realized is controlled by the competition between intervalley Hund's coupling and spin-orbit coupling, and we identify experimental signatures to distinguish them. For a superconducting junction formed across the wall, we further show that the superconducting phase difference couples directly to the intervalley-coherent phase of the texture, allowing precession of this internal phase to generate a voltage. This mechanism provides an explanation for the resistive domain walls recently observed in chiral superconductors [arXiv2605.13303] and predicts accompanying magnetization oscillations that could be detected using GHz-frequency AC probes. Our theory establish a microscopic connection between multicomponent magnetic textures, their internal dynamics, and superconducting transport.
item.dc:creator: Mainak Das, Nemin Wei, Chunli Huang

item.title: The First Magic Angle Beyond the Chiral Limit in Twisted Bilayer Graphene
item.description: arXiv:2609.08347v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a squared-Hamiltonian description of twisted bilayer graphene beyond the chiral limit to explain why the first magic angle remains robust under lattice relaxation, while higher-order magic angles are strongly destabilized. Starting from the non-chiral Bistritzer--MacDonald model with finite same-sublattice tunneling, we show that lattice relaxation reshapes the effective confinement landscape rather than acting as a simple perturbation of the chiral theory. A central result is that the realistic relaxation-renormalized tunneling ratio lies close to a special confinement point where the oscillatory part of the symmetric confinement potential nearly cancels. This places realistic twisted bilayer graphene near a nearly uniform confinement regime. At the same time, finite same-sublattice tunneling activates an additional inter-sublattice current-like channel that competes with the chiral orbital channel. The first magic angle survives because these confinement and current-like contributions remain balanced, whereas higher-order magic angles lose this balance through stronger remote-band hybridization and enhanced real-space localization around AA regions. Our results provide a single-particle mechanism for the breakdown of the chiral magic-angle hierarchy and clarify why the experimentally relevant first magic angle remains the most stable remnant of the chiral flat-band structure.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo A. Navarro-Labastida, Pierre A. Pantaleon, Francisco Guinea, Gerardo G. Naumis

item.title: Interplay of Kekul\'e order, flat bands and electron-phonon coupling in graphene
item.description: arXiv:2609.11711v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Kekul\'{e} order in graphene is known to coexist with both an extended flat band near the van Hove singularity (VHS) and enhanced electron-phonon coupling. However, the microscopic origin of this interplay is still not fully understood. Here, this behavior is traced to the Kekul\'{e}-induced bond distortion and the resulting redistribution of electronic delocalization. In this picture, the conduction band below the VHS is observed to flatten with increasing Kekul\'{e} order, extending its intrinsically weakly dispersive region around the saddle point over a broader momentum range. In parallel, the VHS and dimensionless electron-phonon coupling exhibit approximately quadratic upward responses. The resulting enhancement of the electron-phonon coupling is found to be predominantly governed by the increasing density of states, with the effective deformation potential remaining weakly affected by the distortion. As such, the obtained results are consistent with previous theoretical and experimental studies, while also pointing toward the narrowing of the conduction band and a possible departure of the electron-phonon coupling from the conventional adiabatic regime. Altogether, they highlight the potential of controlled Kekul\'{e} ordering for engineering emergent correlated quantum phases in graphene.
item.dc:creator: Dominik Szcz\c{e}\'sniak

item.title: Visualizing Chiral Edge Modes in Twisted Cuprate Superconductors via Scanning-Probe Quantum Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2609.13070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, unconventional superconductivity hosted by twisted van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures has received immense interest due to the exotic pairing symmetry, electronic interactions and nontrivial topological nature that are naturally relevant to the fast-advancing quantum technologies. Here, we report scanning-probe quantum sensing of nanoscale electromagnetic behaviors of twisted vdW cuprate superconductors. Using single-spin relaxometry, we directly visualize edge modes spontaneously formed in twisted Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x (BSCCO). By investigating temperature dependent variations of edge-state-induced quantum spin relaxation, we experimentally evaluate the magnitude of nontrivial topological band gap opened at nodal points in twisted BSCCO and its critical temperature behaviors under different twist angles. We further observe alternating chiral domains defined by edge modes, exploring experimental signatures of in-plane magnetic field-induced topology in 45{\deg} twisted BSCCO. Our results advance the current understanding of twisted vdW nodal superconductors, presenting an appealing high-temperature topological superconducting material platform for cutting-edge quantum innovation.
item.dc:creator: Senlei Li, Xiaomeng Cui, Renzhi Sun, Lingjie Zhou, Yiran Zhao, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Genda Gu, Hailong Wang, Kartiek Agarwal, Philip Kim, Chunhui Rita Du

item.title: Interlayer coupling between twisted graphenes through atomically-precise barriers
item.description: arXiv:2609.36703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding and controlling interlayer coupling in van der Waals (vdW) materials is crucial for engineering novel electronic phenomena, including correlated states, topological phases, and superconductivity. Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) offers a highly tunable platform to explore how interlayer orientation and separation influence quantum transport and moir\'e physics. Here, we introduce a method for achieving precise, atomic-scale control of interlayer coupling in TBG using dual-gated devices separated by ultrathin, thickness-tunable hBN spacers. This approach enables systematic control of interlayer interactions, demonstrating that the critical displacement field required for electron-hole bilayer behavior decreases as the layer separation increases at a fixed twist angle. Remarkably, at small twist angles, moir\'e-related side peaks persist even when layers are separated by tetralayers of hBN (approximately 1.3 nm), indicating robust interlayer band hybridization. By combining atomic-layer-precise control of interlayer coupling with independent twist angle tunability, our platform opens new avenues for discovering novel moir\'e physics governed by engineered interlayer coupling and moir\'e patterns.
item.dc:creator: Yueyang Wang, Ben Fuller, Hongxia Xue, Tianyu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Vladimir Fal'ko, Dong-Keun Ki

item.title: Quantization through dissipation: impurity states and the optical quantum Hall effect
item.description: arXiv:2609.40337v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The integer quantum Hall effect remains the most paradigmatic and remarkable example of exact quantization in condensed matter physics. Its Hall conductivity $\sigma_{xy}$ is fixed to $e^2/h$ times an integer to a precision limited only by measurement and independent of disorder or interactions. This robustness has several explanations, each capturing a strikingly different piece of the physics. In Laughlin's gauge argument, flux insertion pumps an integer charge between edges, so quantization follows from gauge invariance alone. The edge-channel picture instead attributes transport to chiral, ballistic 1D channels at the sample boundary, one per filled Landau level. Bulk arguments tie $\sigma_{xy}$ to a topological invariant of the disordered system, with extended states compensating exactly for the current not carried by localized ones. Here we demonstrate an additional route to understanding quantization, rooted in the finite-frequency dissipative electrodynamics of the bulk. Using high-precision terahertz Faraday rotation and numerics, we show that the cyclotron resonance alone does not give quantized plateaus under Kramers-Kronig transformation. Quantization is recovered only once a faint, low-frequency, topologically enforced dissipative contribution from impurity states is included. This dynamical mechanism, hiding in plain sight within the dissipative response, ties the DC value to the finite-frequency optical response and offers a new route to quantization through the optical Hall effect, complementary to previous pictures.
item.dc:creator: Zhenisbek Tagay, Ahmed Abouelkomsan, Yugo Onishi, Adbhut Gupta, Loren Pfeiffer, Liang Fu, N. P. Armitage

item.title: Anisotropic Friedel oscillations and isoperimetric transport in two-dimensional free lattice Fermi seas
item.description: arXiv:2610.04724v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two physical consequences of the recent topological classification of 2d Fermi seas for free particles based on flat orbifolds $\mathbb{R}^2/\Gamma$ of discrete symmetry $\Gamma$, are explored. The first is a study of the spatial density behavior inside the mesoscopic window enclosed by the Fermi and (infinite) thermal lengths. It is shown that the single-particle density matrix exhibits a sharp directional anisotropy, encoding a real space diffraction pattern, {\it i.e.}, a Fraunhofer-like diagram of the Fermi sea, that reveals the point-group symmetries of the background lattice $\Gamma$ in the form of anisotropic Friedel oscillations. As examples, the special cases of the $p4m$ and $p6m$ crystallographic flat orbifolds are treated in some detail. The second physical consequence is the establishment of an explicit geometric correspondence between momentum-space packing and electrical transport. A mean-field expression for the longitudinal electrical conductivity $\sigma_{xx}$ as a function of the {\it isoperimetric parameter} $\cal{I}$ of the occupied orbifold domain by utilizing geometric measure theory is presented, satisfiying the scaling law $ \sigma_{xx} \propto 1/\sqrt{\cal{I}}$. The topological transport formula naturally incorporates the vanishing conductivity ($\sigma_{xx} \to 0$) of the previously described ``geometric insulators,'' promoting the isoperimetric parameter as an efficient descriptor for topological and geometric phases in conductors.
item.dc:creator: Guillermo R. Zemba

item.title: Density Functional Theory for 2D Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides with Extended Hubbard Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.05496v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate modelling of the band-edge electronic structure of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), such as MoS$_2$, is essential for understanding their optical, electronic and spintronic properties and enabling future applications. Here, we supplement the standard PBE exchange-correlation functional with on-metal ($U$) and metal--chalcogen ($V$) Hubbard corrections, which can control the orbital composition of band-edge states and consequently improve the quantitative accuracy of various properties. For MoS$_2$, MoSe$_2$, WS$_2$, and WSe$_2$, we optimise the $U$ and $V$ parameters by comparison with experimentally measured spin--orbit splittings at the conduction and valence band edges, and show that these optimal choices also improve agreement of the computed band gap, and ferroelectric potential drop in rhombohedral bilayers, with experimentally measured values. This provides a highly efficient, scalable framework for quantitatively accurate, high-throughput calculations of monolayer and multilayer TMDs, suitable for implementation in 2D-materials databases, as well as large-scale electronic and spintronic device modelling.
item.dc:creator: Xue Li, Suad Alshammari, Igor Rozhansky, James G. McHugh, Vladimir Fal'ko

item.title: Negative charging energy in LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ quantum dots induced by SrTiO$_3$ polarization
item.description: arXiv:2610.07878v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a microscopic mechanism for the negative charging energy in LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ quantum dots, arising from the electrostatic image charge associated with the paraelectric response of SrTiO$_3$. Using a self-consistent configuration-interaction approach that accounts for both Coulomb repulsion and image-charge interactions, we find a robust regime of electron pairing whose strength is tunable through the confinement potential and the effective image-charge distance, set by the thickness of the interfacial two-dimensional electron gas. Our results establish dielectric image-charge effects as a route to controllable electron pairing in oxide quantum dots and other materials with a strong dielectric response.
item.dc:creator: J. Czarnecki, A. Sierant, B. Szafran, P. Szumniak, T. S. Jespersen, G. Meucci, T. Jansen, R. Citro, A. Maiellaro, N. Bergeal, M. Bibes, M. Salluzzo, A. Kalaboukhov, P. W\'ojcik

item.title: Quasiparticle-resolved variational theory of Andreev spin qubits
item.description: arXiv:2610.08557v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An Andreev spin qubit stores a single unpaired spin, yet its coupling to the superconducting phase can be dominated by coherent virtual quasiparticle pairs. We develop a continuum variational description of the odd-parity doublet in a quantum-dot Josephson junction with Coulomb interaction and spin-dependent background tunneling. Retaining configurations with up to two Bogoliubov quasiparticles provides compact analytical expressions for energies and wavefunctions. We benchmark the results against numerical renormalization group calculations and identify sources of error. We obtain closed-form expressions for the conventional and spin-dependent Josephson couplings. Despite their small probability, two-quasiparticle configurations, through coherence with the zero-quasiparticle component, supply exactly half of the leading spin-dependent Josephson coupling even without Coulomb repulsion and dominate it as the repulsion grows. Spin-orbit-induced spin transfer between the dot and the leads produces a Josephson-current contribution that is common to both qubit states and finite at zero phase bias when the dot and lead Zeeman energies differ. We also map the localization of the virtual quasiparticles and the spin density in the leads. The results connect strongly correlated quantum-dot models to effective Hamiltonians used for Andreev-spin-qubit circuits and clarify how the wavefunction structure determines their couplings.
item.dc:creator: Teodor Ili\v{c}in, Rok \v{Z}itko

item.title: Fermion-fermion interaction driven phase transitions in rhombohedral trilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2406.01877v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The effects of short-range fermion-fermion interactions on the low-energy properties of rhombohedral trilayer graphene are comprehensively investigated using the momentum-shell renormalization group method. We take into account all one-loop corrections and establish the energy-dependent coupled evolutions of independent fermionic couplings that carry the physical information stemming from the interplay of various fermion-fermion interactions. With detailed numerical analysis, we observe that the ferocious competition among all fermion-fermion interactions can drive fermionic couplings to four distinct fixed points, dubbed $\textrm{FP}_{1}$, $\textrm{FP}_{2}$, $\textrm{FP}_{3}$, and $\textrm{FP}_{4}$, in the interaction-parameter space. These fixed points primarily dictate the fate of the system in the low-energy regime and are always associated with some instabilities characterized by specific symmetry breakings, leading to certain phase transitions. To determine the favorable states arising from the potential phase transitions, we introduce a number of fermion-bilinear source terms to characterize the underlying candidate states. By comparing their related susceptibilities, we find that the dominant states correspond to spin-singlet superconductivity, spin-triplet pair-density-waves, and spin-triplet superconductivity for fixed points $\textrm{FP}_{1,3}$, $\textrm{FP}_{2}$, and $\textrm{FP}_{4}$, respectively. These provide valuable insights into the low-energy properties of rhombohedral trilayer graphene and analogous materials.
item.dc:creator: Qiao-Chu Zhang, Jing Wang

item.title: A General Framework for Gradient-Based Optimization of Superconducting Quantum Circuits using Qubit Discovery as a Case Study
item.description: arXiv:2408.12704v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Engineering the Hamiltonian of a quantum system is fundamental to the design of quantum systems. Automating Hamiltonian design through gradient-based optimization can dramatically accelerate this process. However, computing the gradients of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a Hamiltonian--a large, sparse matrix--relative to system properties poses a significant challenge, especially for arbitrary systems. Superconducting quantum circuits offer substantial flexibility in Hamiltonian design, making them an ideal platform for this task. In this work, we present a comprehensive framework for the gradient-based optimization of superconducting quantum circuits, leveraging the SQcircuit software package. By addressing the challenge of calculating the gradient of the eigensystem for large, sparse Hamiltonians and integrating automatic differentiation within SQcircuit, our framework enables efficient and precise computation of gradients for various circuit properties or custom-defined metrics, streamlining the optimization process. We apply this framework to the qubit discovery problem, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying qubit designs with superior performance metrics. The optimized circuits show improvements in a heuristic measure of gate count, upper bounds on gate speed, decoherence time, and resilience to noise and fabrication errors compared to existing qubits. While this methodology is showcased through qubit optimization and discovery, it is versatile and can be extended to tackle other optimization challenges in superconducting quantum hardware design.
item.dc:creator: Taha Rajabzadeh, Alex Boulton-McKeehan, Sam Bonkowsky, David I. Schuster, Amir H. Safavi-Naeini

item.title: Extreme Suppression of Thermal Conductivity in Monolayer Beryllene
item.description: arXiv:2409.05766v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We demonstrate an extreme suppression of thermal conductivity in monolayer beryllene through first-principles solutions of the phonon Boltzmann transport equation. While the fully converged three-phonon calculation predicts a room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity of 154.3 W/(m$\cdot$K), inclusion of four-phonon interactions suppresses it to 10.7 W/(m$\cdot$K), a reduction of more than 90\%. This exceptionally large reduction of the thermal conductivity is amongst the highest reported in two-dimensional materials. The microscopic origin of this breakdown is traced to the strong sensitivity of the low-frequency flexural ZA phonons to four-phonon scattering: mode-resolved scattering rates reveal a pronounced enhancement of ZA scattering, which substantially shortens their lifetimes and suppresses their dominant contribution to heat conduction. Moreover, the temperature dependence of the thermal conductivity changes from $\kappa\propto T^{-0.86}$ to $\kappa\propto T^{-1.38}$ upon inclusion of four-phonon processes. Our results establish $\alpha$-beryllene as an unusually strong case of four-phonon-controlled thermal transport amongst two-dimensional materials. These findings identify selective higher-order scattering of flexural phonons as a key mechanism for controlling thermal transport in strongly anharmonic low-dimensional systems.
item.dc:creator: Sapta Sindhu Paul Chowdhury, Santosh Mogurampelly

item.title: peaks: a Python package for analysis of angle-resolved photoemission and related spectroscopies
item.description: arXiv:2508.04803v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The electronic band structure, describing the motion and interactions of electrons in materials, dictates the electrical, optical, and thermodynamic properties of solids. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) provides a direct experimental probe of such electronic band structures, and so is widely employed in the study of functional, quantum, and 2D materials. \texttt{peaks} (\textbf{P}ython \textbf{E}lectron spectroscopy \textbf{A}nalysis by \textbf{K}ing group @ \textbf{S}t Andrews) provides a Python package for advanced data analysis of ARPES and related spectroscopic data. It facilitates the fast visualisation and analysis of multi-dimensional datasets, allows for the complex data hierarchy typical to ARPES experiments, and supports lazy data loading and parallel processing, reflecting the ever-increasing data volumes used in ARPES. It is designed to be run in an interactive notebook environment, with extensive inline and pop-out GUI support for data visualisation.
item.dc:creator: Phil D. C. King, Brendan Edwards, Shu Mo, Tommaso Antonelli, Edgar Abarca Morales, Lewis Hart, Liam Trzaska

item.title: The Arf-Brown-Kervaire invariant on a lattice
item.description: arXiv:2512.11424v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a lattice formulation of the Arf-Brown-Kervaire (ABK) invariant which takes values in $\mathbb{Z}_8$. Compared to the standard $\mathbb{Z}$-valued index, the ABK invariant is more involved in that it arises in Majorana fermion partition functions with reflection symmetry on two-dimensional non-orientable manifolds, and its definition contains an infinite sum over Dirac eigenvalues that requires proper regularization. We employ the massive Wilson Dirac operator, with and without domain-walls, on standard two-dimensional square lattices, and use its Pfaffian for the definition. Twisted boundary conditions and cross-caps, which reverse the orientation, are introduced to realize nontrivial topologies equipped with nontrivial $\mathrm{Pin}^{-}$ structures of Majorana fermions. We verify numerically (and partly analytically) that our formulation on a torus, Klein bottle, real projective plane (as well as its triple connected sum), and two types of M\"obius strip reproduces the known values in continuum theory.

item.title: Active fluctuations drive inertia-free absolute negative mobility in soft and living matter
item.description: arXiv:2603.06070v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Absolute negative mobility (ANM) is one of the most paradoxical transport phenomena in which a setup moves on average in a direction opposite to the applied force. The simplest system exhibiting this effect in minimal one-dimensional dynamics involves an inertial particle subjected to a constant bias while dwelling in a nonlinear, symmetric periodic potential in a nonequilibrium, nonstationary state generated by external driving. The necessity of inertia poses a significant conceptual barrier in predicting the ANM in a microscopic world of soft and living matter such as biological cells. In this work, we solve a two-decade old puzzle and demonstrate that none of the previously thought factors required for this effect are decisive. We show that the ANM may occur in a system composed of an overdamped particle in a piecewise linear symmetric periodic potential in an equilibrium state, provided that it is additionally driven by active fluctuations in the form of white Poisson shot noise. Our result may help to explain exotic transport behaviour emerging in biological cells where dynamics is typically overdamped and assisted by active fluctuations derived from various metabolic activities. It can also be exploited for effective separation strategies in a microscopic world, thus transforming fluctuations from a nuisance into a functional resource.
item.dc:creator: K. Bia{\l}as, P. H\"anggi, J. Spiechowicz

item.title: Unambiguous characterization of in-plane dielectric response in nanoconfined liquids: water as a case study
item.description: arXiv:2604.00700v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The in-plane dielectric constant of nanoconfined water has attracted growing interest in recent years. Nevertheless, assigning a bulk-like dielectric constant to a molecularly thin film is convention dependent because it requires choosing an effective water width. We propose the in-plane 2D polarizability, $\alpha_{\parallel}$, as a macroscopic characterization of the in-plane dielectric response that avoids this choice. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we compute $\alpha_{\parallel}$ via two independent and consistent methods: based on fluctuation--dissipation theory, and from the induced dipole moment when water is placed in a capacitor. Our results provide the framework to quantify the in-plane dielectric response of polar liquids across simulations and experiments.

item.title: Double circular dichroism high harmonic spectroscopy: An ultrafast probe for topological photocurrents
item.description: arXiv:2604.21121v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding optical responses of topological matter is central to optoelectronic applications, photocurrent control, and spectroscopy. Yet schemes for sensing ultrafast photocurrents and separating bulk and surface contributions are lacking. We introduce double circular dichroism (DCD) harmonic spectroscopy as an all-optical probe of ultrafast dynamics in topological materials. Pump and probe pulses are circular with independently controlled helicities, yielding the circular dichroism of the circular dichroism: a time-resolved response that evaluates how probe-induced dichroism depends on pump helicity. While DCD vanishes in symmetric systems, it survives in broken time-reversal-symmetry materials, including Chern insulators. Simulations in a Haldane nanoflake, where a pump manipulates chiral current-carrying states and intense probe pulses drive harmonic emission, show that DCD arises from bulk and edge-localized states with opposite signs, similar magnitudes, and different amplitude scaling. Edge-associated DCD is connected to the outermost atomic layer of exponentially localized protected modes and is relatively robust to bulk-edge interference, enabling separation of bulk and edge photocurrents. Varying the electronic structure and laser parameters reveals harmonic anomalies that may probe topological attributes of photocurrents and material phase. In particular, HHG DCD oscillations under band-structure manipulation vary strongly across the phase transition and become stable and nonoscillatory in topologically trivial phases. DCD also oscillates with pump-probe delay on attosecond timescales, offering an ultrafast probe of topological photocurrents and their coherence. DCD could therefore disentangle bulk and boundary photoresponses in broken-symmetry quantum and topological matter and be implemented in photoelectron and absorption pump-probe spectroscopies and chiral systems.

item.title: Lieb-Schultz-Mattis constraints for hyperbolic lattices
item.description: arXiv:2605.15974v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Lieb-Schultz-Mattis (LSM) theorem and its higher-dimensional extensions forbid the existence of a unique, symmetric, and gapped ground state at fractional fillings in quantum many-body systems with a conserved particle number (or spin angular momentum) and the conventional translation symmetry of Euclidean lattices. In this work, we propose a generalization of the LSM theorem to quantum many-body systems on hyperbolic lattices, i.e., regular tessellations of two-dimensional negatively curved space. By leveraging concepts from hyperbolic band theory in a many-body setting, we adapt Oshikawa's flux-threading argument to periodic hyperbolic lattices with a non-Euclidean (Fuchsian) translation symmetry and compute a lower-bound to the ground-state degeneracy as a function of filling and lattice geometry. We explore the consequences of LSM constraints for gapped phases of hyperbolic quantum matter and suggest frustrated spin models on hyperbolic analogs of the square and triangular lattices as promising platforms for realizing symmetric spin liquids in hyperbolic space.

item.title: Quantum critical collapse of a pinned vortex glass in high-field superconducting resonators
item.description: arXiv:2605.23838v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The interplay between disorder and vortex--vortex interactions in strongly disordered superconductors in a magnetic field can stabilize a vortex-glass state, characterized by strong pinning and the absence of positional order. Yet its role in the destruction of superconductivity at the field-driven superconductor--insulator transition has remained unresolved. Here we use plasmonic microwave spectroscopy of superconducting resonators patterned from amorphous indium oxide thin films to directly track the superfluid density up to the critical field $B_c$. We find an unexpected resilience of the superfluid density, which decreases only logarithmically over nearly three orders of magnitude in field, in stark contrast to the rapid power-law suppression expected for vortex lattices. We attribute this anomalously slow decay to a collective vortex-pinning mechanism counterintuitively enhanced by vortex--vortex interactions. The superfluid density then vanishes linearly at $B_c$, where independent magnetoresistance measurements identify a continuous quantum critical point, unlike the abrupt transition observed at zero field. We further uncover an exceptionally large nonlinear electromagnetic response of the vortex glass, manifested as a pronounced positive-Kerr effect with potential for quantum sensing. These results show how disorder controls the critical magnetic field and identify the vortex glass as the key intermediate state governing the magnetic-field-induced superconductor--insulator transition.

item.title: Helical Dirac Current with Local Coupling to a Chiral Potential
item.description: arXiv:2606.17618v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that a propagating electron wave in the lowest cylindrical channel carries a spin-resolved helical conserved current, and connect this current texture to its local chiral coupling. In a weakly relativistic positive-energy Dirac projection, the two sectors have the same azimuthally symmetric charge density and opposite circulation superposed on longitudinal flow, even though their nonrelativistic orbital harmonic is $l=0$. The current is radially distributed and extends into the evanescent tail. A scalar screw potential couples these modes through a derived vertex expressed by the \emph{chiral current overlap}, $\mathcal J_\chi$. Both spatial textures determine the coupling: the environmental radial profile weights the electronic circulation, while the screw harmonic selects correlated changes of spin sector and longitudinal momentum. For a uniform static harmonic, elastic energy conservation makes the first-order spin-flip amplitude vanish within the same transverse mode. Environmental energy exchange is therefore required to activate these selected channels. The same current overlap supplies the spatial kernel for heliciton-assisted inelastic scattering in a companion study and for a subsequent transport treatment of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS).

item.title: Fluctuation-dissipation structure of quantum geometry
item.description: arXiv:2608.25006v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Geometry of quantum states is a fundamental research area with applications ranging from topological materials in condensed matter to variational algorithms in quantum information. Due to their relative simplicity, pure states are often studied, while mixed states are generally needed, for instance to have nonzero temperatures or other statistical mixtures. Mixed-state geometry, however, is much more challenging and has so far lacked any overall structure that relates distance and curvature, like the K\"ahler structure does for pure states. This work introduces that missing structure. We show that it has the physical meaning of fluctuation-dissipation---by identifying distance with fluctuations and curvature with linear response---and becomes the known structure for pure states, but is non-K\"ahler otherwise. This paints a simple picture that unifies fluctuation-dissipation and geometry of quantum states. It also applies on parameter spaces, as encountered in condensed matter or estimation theory. Our picture implies that the geometry contains all linear responses and fluctuations, proves the usual fluctuation-dissipation relation, explains that quantum geometry is present in any sum rule, and allows one to geometrically characterize generic transport behaviors.
